REFERRING PHYSICIAN
Dr. [redacted name]
[redacted location] Cancer Center

CLINICAL INDICATION
Predictive testing for Lynch syndrome due to family history. First degree relative with confirmed heterozygous pathogenic variant MSH2 c.1481C>A p.(Ser494Ter).

TEST PERFORMED
Targeted Variant Analysis - MSH2 gene
Methodology: Fluorescent Sanger sequencing for specific familial variant detection
Genomic Coordinates: Chr2(GRCh37):g.47690264C>A

RESULTS

Gene	Transcript	Variant	Zygosity	Classification
MSH2	NM_000251.2	c.1481C>A p.(Ser494Ter)	Not Detected	Pathogenic (familial)

INTERPRETATION
Targeted testing for the familial MSH2 c.1481C>A p.(Ser494Ter) pathogenic variant was performed. This variant was NOT DETECTED in the patient sample.

The MSH2 c.1481C>A variant results in a premature termination codon at position 494 (p.Ser494Ter), leading to nonsense-mediated decay and loss of MSH2 protein function. This variant is classified as pathogenic for Lynch syndrome based on multiple lines of evidence including functional studies and segregation with disease in multiple families.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
The absence of the familial MSH2 pathogenic variant indicates that this individual has not inherited the increased cancer risk associated with this specific variant. Therefore:

• No increased risk for Lynch syndrome-associated cancers (colorectal, endometrial, ovarian, gastric, etc.) attributable to the familial MSH2 variant
• Population-level baseline risk for sporadic cancers remains
• Other familial cancer predisposition risks may still apply if present in the family
• No enhanced cancer surveillance specific to Lynch syndrome is indicated based on this result

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling to discuss test results and implications
2. Standard population-based cancer screening as recommended by primary care physician
3. Predictive testing is available for other at-risk family members with appropriate pre-test genetic counseling
4. Consider evaluation for other hereditary cancer syndromes if additional family history concerns exist

TECHNICAL INFORMATION
Test Methodology: Targeted variant analysis was performed using bidirectional Sanger sequencing. PCR amplification of MSH2 exon 9 was performed using gene-specific primers. Sequencing reactions were performed using BigDye Terminator v3.1 chemistry and analyzed on an Applied Biosystems 3730xl DNA Analyzer. Sequence data was analyzed using Mutation Surveyor software v5.1.2.

Test Limitations: This test is designed to detect only the specific familial variant MSH2 c.1481C>A. Other pathogenic variants in MSH2 or other Lynch syndrome genes would not be detected by this targeted analysis. Rare polymorphisms or technical artifacts may interfere with variant detection.

Quality Metrics:
• Coverage at variant position: >30x bidirectional
• Sequence quality score: >Q30
• PCR amplification: Successful

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
